_comment: Error taxonomy every port exposes as four distinct, matchable error
classes. Messages MUST NOT carry credential values. `oauth_errors` maps
the RFC 6749 section 5.2 `error` code of a token endpoint response;
`other` maps non-OAuth failures. A grant not listed for a code uses the

classes.name: credential_rejected
classes.meaning: Token endpoint refused the credential (bad secret, revoked key, invalid assertion). Retrying cannot help.

classes.name: needs_reconsent
classes.meaning: Grant unusable until the user grants access again (expired or revoked refresh token).

classes.name: not_writable
classes.meaning: Grant needs write-back (refresh token rotation) and the secret backend does not declare itself writable.

classes.name: transient
classes.meaning: Network or server failure. Retrying may succeed.

other.condition: other HTTP 4xx from token endpoint (any error code, or none)
secret store read failure other than not found
rotating grant on a backend without writable declaration

unclassified.condition: HTTP 3xx from token endpoint: redirect refused, never followed
TLS certificate verification failure (unknown authority, invalid or expired certificate, hostname mismatch): configuration fault, retrying cannot help
2xx token response missing access_token or expires_in: retrying cannot help and the credential is not at fault

validation.condition: secret ref not found in the store: validation error naming the ref field
